sections.h2: Where do I record a deed in Prince George's County?
sections.html:
Recording takes two stops in person: the county Office of Finance in Largo, then the Land Records Division of the Circuit Court in Upper Marlboro. The court's deed processing page lays out the order, and the county step comes first.

StepOfficeAddress and hours
1Office of Finance1301 McCormick Drive, Suite 1100, Largo; 301-952-4030; 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. weekdays
2Land Records Division14701 Governor Oden Bowie Drive, Room J1108, Upper Marlboro; 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. weekdays

Bring the original deed, one full copy, and the State of Maryland land instrument intake sheet. A deed that claims an exemption from recording fees or state transfer tax has to cite every applicable code section from the Maryland Annotated Code. The Land Records Division itself answers at 301-780-2253, and the courthouse main line is 301-952-3655.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Prince George's County?
sections.html:
The county's fee page lists $20 for an instrument of 1 to 9 pages, and that fee covers every page when the instrument concerns a principal residence. A $40 surcharge sits on top for recorded documents. The statewide circuit court schedule that takes effect September 2, 2026 lists $60 for a principal residence instrument, so the two sources disagree and the amount should be confirmed by phone.

ServiceCounty fee page
Other instrument, 1 to 9 pages (all pages if principal residence)$20
Other instrument, 10 or more pages, not a principal residence$75
Release, 1 to 9 pages$10
Surcharge on recorded documents (not powers of attorney, plats, chattel)$40
Copy of a deed or other document$2
Copy of a deed of trust or mortgage$5
Certified copy of a deed of trust or mortgage$10
Certified copy, other instruments$7

Payment is due when the document is recorded. The office takes cash, checks, money orders and credit cards, with checks and money orders payable to The Clerk of the Circuit Court. Documents come back by mail when you supply a return address, and otherwise they wait for pickup.

sections.h2: What transfer and recordation taxes apply in Prince George's County?
sections.html:
The county transfer tax is 1.4%, set under County Code sections 10-187 and 10-188, and the state recordation tax is $5.50 per $1,000 of consideration. The county's Finance Affidavit instructions put the recordation figure as $2.75 per $500, rounded up to the next $500, and the state legislative rate table lists the same $2.75. The state transfer tax of 0.5% comes on top.

TaxRateAuthority
County transfer tax1.4%County Code 10-187 and 10-188
Recordation tax$5.50 per $1,000Maryland Tax-Property Article, collected by the county
State transfer tax0.5%, or 0.25% for a qualifying first-time buyerTax-Property 13-203

The court's Land Records page sends questions about the state transfer tax to the Land Records Division and questions about county transfer and recordation tax to the Office of Finance. On a $400,000 sale, 1.4% county transfer tax alone comes to $5,600, so the split between buyer and seller is worth settling in the contract. Maryland's default is an equal split unless the contract or a law says otherwise.

sections.h2: What is the Finance Affidavit, and who needs it?
sections.html:
The Finance Affidavit is the form Prince George's County uses to claim an exemption from the county transfer tax or the state recordation tax. The county says every instrument recorded in its land records is taxable unless Maryland's code or the county code exempts it, and the affidavit is how a filer names the exemption.

Most of its clauses concern loans and refinances:

  • Clause A: a principal residence refinance, where recordation tax applies to the difference between the new loan and the unpaid principal balance.
  • Clause B-1: a principal residence with a purchase money deed of trust recorded for more than 12 months, covering new loans, modifications and home equity lines.
  • Clause B-2: a refinance by a borrower who does not qualify for B-1, paired with Clause A.
  • Clause C: a refinance of a non-principal residence or investment property, where the 1.4% county transfer tax applies to the difference between the new and original loan amounts.

The property must be the borrower's principal residence in state assessment records. The county's instructions list the Treasury as the contact for submission details.

sections.h2: What disclosures does Maryland require for Prince George's County sales?
sections.html:
Prince George's County has its own line items in the state's residential contract statute. Section 14-117 of the Real Property Article requires, where deferred private water and sewer assessments are recorded, that the contract disclose eight items, including the assessment amount, remaining payments, interest rate, payoff amount, and that prepayment carries no penalty. Those assessments cannot be amortized over more than 20 years.

The contract also has to disclose whether a development impact fee was imposed on the property, the total amount, and any unpaid balance. Statewide, every residential sale needs a homestead property tax credit statement, and one- or two-unit contracts need the statement that recordation and transfer taxes are shared equally unless negotiated otherwise.

sections.h2: What kind of place is Prince George's County?
sections.html:
Prince George's County borders Washington, D.C. on its west side, and it was created on April 23, 1696 from parts of Charles and Calvert counties. It covers 499 square miles, 483 of them land, and the 2020 census counted 967,201 residents, which makes it the second-most populous county in Maryland. Upper Marlboro is the county seat, though some government functions have moved to the Largo area since 1991.

U.S. Route 50 roughly divides North and South County. Informal regions include North County, Central County, the Rural Tier, the Inner Beltway and South County. Bowie is the largest city, at 58,329 people in 2020, and other cities and towns include Laurel, College Park, Greenbelt and Hyattsville. Large unincorporated communities include Largo, Clinton, Oxon Hill, Fort Washington and National Harbor.

The county has the only Potomac River waterfront in Maryland, and the Patuxent River forms its eastern border. The western edge near Montgomery County rises into the Piedmont above 300 feet, while most of the county is Atlantic Coastal Plain with gently rolling hills.

sections.h2: Who are the big employers and how do people get around?
sections.html:
Federal and university jobs lead the 2021 employer list on Wikipedia:

  • Joint Base Andrews, 18,000 jobs
  • University System of Maryland, 13,000
  • NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, 12,200
  • University of Maryland Capital Region Health, 4,800
  • IRS, 4,500, and the U.S. Census Bureau, 4,285
  • UPS, 3,300, and MGM National Harbor, 2,400

The Washington Metro has 15 stations in the county, including terminals at Greenbelt, New Carrollton, Largo and Branch Avenue. MARC's Camden and Penn lines also serve it, TheBus runs county routes, and a water taxi leaves from National Harbor. The Purple Line is slated to open in 2027. Reagan National, BWI and Dulles are the nearby airports. The school system is Prince George's County Public Schools.

sections.h2: What property tax facts matter to a Prince George's County seller?
sections.html:
The county real property rate is $1.0000 per $100 of assessed value for fiscal 2026, the county Treasury says, with the state adding $0.1120 and Park and Planning adding $0.2940. The county's Tax Facts sheet says unpaid taxes can lead to a lien sold at the annual tax sale on the second Monday in May.

The county caps the taxable assessment increase for fiscal 2026 at 3%, while the state cap is 10% after the first full tax year. In the state's 2024 tax sale survey, Prince George's County advertised 4,283 properties, offered 2,206, and sold 2,003 liens, while 1,146 properties were redeemed before foreclosure in fiscal 2024. The county's Homeowner Protection Program may keep a limited-income home out of tax sale for at least three years, though enrollment is limited.

faqs.q: Where is the Prince George's County land records office?
faqs.a: The Land Records Division is in the Judiciary Administrative Services Building at 14701 Governor Oden Bowie Drive, Room J1108, in Upper Marlboro. It is open 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays.

faqs.q: Do I pay the county first or the court first?
faqs.a: The county Office of Finance in Largo comes first, then the Land Records Division in Upper Marlboro. Call 301-952-4030 for the Finance step.

faqs.q: What is the Prince George's County transfer tax rate?
faqs.a: It is 1.4% under County Code 10-187 and 10-188. The state also charges a 0.5% transfer tax and a recordation tax of $5.50 per $1,000.

faqs.q: Can I search Prince George's County land records online?
faqs.a: Yes. The court points to the Land Records Online Search at landrec.msa.maryland.gov, which shows recorded and verified land records volumes. Clerks cannot give legal advice or run title searches.

faqs.q: Why do two sources show different recording fees?
faqs.a: The county fee page lists $20 for a principal residence instrument, while the statewide schedule effective September 2, 2026 lists $60. Call 301-780-2253 to confirm the current amount before you record.
